questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- very different enviroment
- interstering biology
- litlle community => thus easy to get to know people

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yhe UNIS website is very good and easy to get around in. furhtermore samskipnaden (the housing portal) is easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reception at unis is always ready to help you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: very easy - elvesletta is were almost everybody lives.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: elvesletta almost dont count as "off campus" because its such a small city and everybody you know is living there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The applying it self was fairly easy. But as stated above the information pr. made the applying unnecessarily hard because you had to be in contact with two different institutions. Thus this was a bit hectic.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The institutions was good at answering at emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: successful. i got into all the classes i applyied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it and be patient. Some of my classmates got in on waitinglists. some of them even only got in a week before the course started

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses level was suitable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching depended very much of the teacher from the course. The first course was with a danish teacher, thus the teaching style was very much what i was used to. 
the other two couses i had was with resp. a german and norwegian teacher that dident car so much about breaks. this was quit a cultural chok as i am very fond of the 45 min 15 break method.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AB-333 Freshwater Ecology of Arctic Lakes and Ponds
AB-329 Arctic Winter Ecology
AB-323 Light Climate and Primary Productivity in the Arctic

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
AB-333 Freshwater Ecology of Arctic Lakes and Ponds: good planning, good teching, and really good field work. 
AB-323 Light Climate and Primary Productivity in the Arctic: new interesting methods, going to Ny Ålesund on field trip, interesting subject.

questions.answer: Food and gear is expensive in svalbard

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Climbing, svimming, gym, hikes, skiing, friday gathering etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on scooter trips and hikes!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: as mentioned above

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy. people are super open and friendly. Also everybody is international and comes from abroad with makes is more easy to get friends quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: its really just to be open to all arrangment happening. also living in elveletta (the student housing) and a shared kitchen makes it happen by itself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
the dark/light season with 24 h light or darknesss makes it hard to sleep. 
Being around people all the time if you are not used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The socializing, and the beautiful nature that you spend a lot of time in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring warm clothing (woolen underwear is key). 
Bye a scooter if you are there for 6 month. its worth it and give alot of possiblities and freedom. 
Go checkout the sauna.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Also remember "normal" cloth and not only outdoor cloth, as there is also many bars and parties to attend.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The people and the friends i made. 
also all the wonderfull nature experiences! its incredible how beautiful it is.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was to keep concentration on my school work. especially in the end of the semester because you know you are going home soon and that the friends you made wont be in your home country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
